frase_gancho.texto: From the milpa to the kitchen: how food is produced and shared.

introduccion_narrativa.texto: This hall is about what is planted, worked and eaten. It shows how Indigenous peoples produce their food and trade it, and how maize, fire and kitchens order daily life. Here you will find a Purépecha granary where the harvest is kept, utensils made of ixtle, copper and black clay, and two murals that show the landscape food comes from: a Purépecha wedding and the valleys of the Mezquital and Toluca. On this museum’s upper floor, eating is not only feeding yourself: it is a way of being together.
